implementation_notes: Ruby's poltergeist is usually a class in `app/helpers/` whose single method manipulates a view or a model — which is the exact case the practitioner discussion raises with `DialogHelper#addWelcomeDialog` and the natural home of `MyView`. The idiomatic Ruby answers are a view helper method on the view's own helper module, a plain module function, or a concern when the behaviour genuinely belongs to several classes. What to avoid is the standard Rails rescue: moving the method into `ApplicationHelper`, which is a god helper with no owner.
idiom_name: helper object with only initialize + one method
pitfalls: `ApplicationHelper` is the standard rescue and produces a god helper accumulating every helper method ever written.
A `Service` object created per call with one method is a poltergeist with a respectable name.
`concern` used to justify the helper is the wrong tool: it keeps the method on the same class while adding a module.
